key_insight: A context-aware Markov decision process can personalize Type 2 diabetes follow-up intervals by combining patient trajectories and risk profiles, outperforming fixed-interval care plans.
engineering_relevance: This work shows how probabilistic decision models and EHR-derived contexts can support adaptive, data-driven care scheduling in clinical decision support systems.
method: Extract patient trajectory features from EHR data using principal component analysis.
Cluster patients into risk contexts using principal components plus patient-level features.
Learn CMDP policies to choose follow-up intervals based on visit state and context.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 22,154 T2D patients from 10 primary care clinics, with CMDP policies lowering expected cumulative cost versus an ADA-like fixed-interval benchmark by about 34.8% in the higher-comorbidity context and 6.4% in the lower-comorbidity context.
watch_item: Deployment may be limited by EHR data quality, context drift across clinics, and the need for clinician oversight before changing guideline-based follow-up schedules.
paper_title: Context-Aware Optimization of Follow-Up Intervals for Type 2 Diabetes Care Using Markov Decision Processes
